Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 62–63:

﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then surely Allah is sufficient for you﴾. Then, indeed, your sufficiency (ḥasb) is Allah, and your Protector (kāfī). Jarir said:

I have found, among the noble qualities, that it is sufficient for you (ḥasbukum) that you wear the noble garments and be satisfied.

﴿It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾ all together.

﴿And He joined their hearts﴾ despite what was among them of tribal partisanship (ʿaṣabiyyah) and rancour over the slightest matter, and their eagerness for revenge, to the extent that hardly would two hearts among them come together, until they became as one soul. This is among his miracles (ﷺ). Its clarification is: ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts﴾, meaning: their enmity had reached such a degree that if a spender had spent on reconciling their affairs all the wealth that is in the earth (p-66), he would not have been able to achieve harmony and reconciliation. ﴿But Allah joined them together﴾ by His perfect power, for He is the Owner of hearts; He turns them however He wills. ﴿Indeed He is Mighty﴾, possessing complete power and dominance, such that what He wills cannot be disobeyed. ﴿Wise﴾, knowing how what He wills ought to be done. It has been said that the verse concerns the Aws and the Khazraj, among whom there were endless afflictions and battles in which their chieftains perished; then Allah caused them to forget that and joined them together through Islam, until they became pure of heart and became the Ansar (Helpers).

O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you (ﷺ)—﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ﴾ meaning: He is sufficient for you (ḥasbuka: "sufficient," i.e., protecting and suffices you). ﴿وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ("and whoever follows you of the believers") may be in the accusative position as an object with "with" (maf'ūl maʿahu), as in his saying:

*When war blazes and spears interlace, then sufficient for you (are) al-Ḍaḥḥāk and a sharp Indian sword.*

Or it may be in the genitive by conjunction with the pronoun (ʿaṭfan ʿalā al-maknī), according to the Kufans; or in the nominative by conjunction with the name of Allah the Exalted, meaning: Allah and the believers suffice you.

The verse was revealed at al-Bayḍāʾ during the expedition of Badr. It is said that there had embraced Islam with the Prophet (ﷺ) thirty-three men and six women, then ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) embraced Islam, and the verse was revealed. For this reason Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said: it was revealed concerning his conversion.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 65–66:

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾. He pressed them hard to it (bālagha fī ḥathhihim ʿalayhi). Its root is ḥaraḍ, which is when illness wears a person down until he is near death (yashfī ʿalā al-mawt). It is also read "ḥarriṣ" (ḥarriṣ), from ḥirṣ (greed, eagerness). ﴿If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve﴾. This is a conditional sentence carrying the sense of a command to the one to endure against ten, and the promise that if they are steadfast they will prevail by the help and support of God. Ibn Kathir, Nafi< and Ibn ʿAmir read "takun" (with the tā') in both verses, and the two Basrans agreed with them in "wa-in takun minkum mi'atun" (and if there are a hundred of you). ﴿Because they are a people who do not understand﴾, that is, because they are ignorant of God and the Last Day, and do not hold firm for the reward of the believers and the lofty ranks, whether they kill or are killed; and they deserve from God nothing but humiliation and abandonment.

﴿Now God has lightened your burden and knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are a hundred of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand, by God's permission﴾. When He had obligated the one to withstand ten and to stand firm against them, and that was burdensome to them, He lightened it for them by making one withstand two. It is said that they were few at the time, so they were commanded thus, and then when they became many, He lightened it for them. The repetition of one meaning with proportionate numbers serves to show that the ruling for the few and the many is the same. "Weakness" (ḍaʿf) here is weakness of body. It is also said it is weakness of insight, and they varied in it. There are two dialectal forms: with a fatha (al-fatḥ), which is the reading of ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza, and with a ḍamma (al-ḍamm), which is the reading of the rest. ﴿And God is with the steadfast﴾, with victory and help; so how could they not overcome?

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 67:

﴿It is not for a Prophet﴾ It is also read as "لِلنَّبِيِّ" (lil-nabiyyi, "for the Prophet"), with the definite article indicating a specific, known reference (al-'ahd). ﴿that he should have captives﴾ The two Basran reciters (al-Basriyyan) read it with a "ta'" (tu'), "تَكُونَ" (takuna), instead of "yakuna". ﴿until he has thoroughly subdued [the enemy] in the land﴾ That is, he should kill extensively and go to great lengths in doing so, until disbelief is humbled, its party is diminished, Islam is strengthened, and its people gain control. It derives from "athkhanahu al-marad" (the illness weighed him down), meaning "when it burdened him," and its root is thickness (al-thakhanah). It is also read as "yuthakhkhina" (with shaddah), for emphasis. ﴿you desire the goods of this world﴾ That is, its fleeting wealth, by your taking ransom (al-fida').

﴿But Allah desires the Hereafter﴾ That is, He desires for you the reward of the Hereafter, or the means of attaining the reward of the Hereafter, through strengthening His religion and suppressing His enemies. It is also read as "al-Akhirati" in the genitive (bi-jarri "al-Akhirah"), by supposing an elided noun (idmar al-mudaf), as in the saying of the poet:

"Is every man you think a man...
and a fire kindled by night, a fire?"

﴿And Allah is Mighty﴾ He overcomes His allies over their enemies. ﴿Wise﴾ He knows what is fitting in every circumstance and specifies it for that circumstance. Thus He commanded thorough subduing and forbade ransom when the might was with the polytheists, and He gave them the choice between ransom and grace (al-mann) when the situation changed and dominance passed to the believers.

It has been narrated that "he (peace be upon him) came on the day of Badr with seventy captives, among them al-'Abbas and 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib. He consulted about them, and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'They are your people and your family; spare them, perhaps Allah will accept their repentance, and take from them a ransom with which to strengthen your companions.' 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Strike their necks, for they are the leaders of disbelief, and Allah has made you independent of ransom. Let me have so-and-so, a relative of mine, and let 'Ali and Hamzah have their brothers, and we will strike their necks.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not favour that, and said: 'Indeed Allah softens the hearts of some men until they are softer than milk, and Allah hardens the hearts of some men until they are harder than stones. And your likeness, O Abu Bakr, is the likeness of Abraham, who said: "Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful" [14:36]. And your likeness, O 'Umar, is the likeness of Noah, who said: "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dwelling" [71:26].' He gave his companions the choice, and they took the ransom. Then this verse was revealed. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and found him and Abu Bakr weeping. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me why you weep, for if I find a reason to weep I will weep, and if not, I will pretend to weep.' He said: 'Weep for your companions over their taking of the ransom. Their punishment was presented to me, as near as this tree' — a nearby tree."

The verse is evidence that the Prophets (peace be upon them) exercise ijtihad (independent reasoning, ijtihad), and that an error may occur in it, but they are not left to persist in it.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 68–69:**

﴿Had there not been a decree from God that had already gone forth﴾: that is, had there not been a ruling from God, already recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), that He would not punish the one who errs in his ijtihad (independent legal reasoning), or that He would not punish the people of Badr, or a people, for something they had not been explicitly forbidden, or that the ransom they took would be lawful for them. ﴿Surely a great punishment would have touched you﴾: would have reached you ﴿for what you took﴾: of the ransom ﴿of great punishment﴾. It is related that he, peace be upon him, said: "Had punishment descended, none would have escaped it except Umar and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

And that is because he (Sa'd) also advised thorough subduing (al-ithkhan, overpowering the enemy thoroughly).

﴿So eat of what you have gained﴾: of the ransom, for it is among the spoils of war. It was said: they had refrained from the spoils, so this was revealed. The fa' (in fa-kulu) is the fa' of causation (li-l-tasabbub), and its cause is omitted; its estimated sense is: "I have made the spoils lawful to you, so eat." It is on this basis that whoever claims that a command following a prohibition signifies permissibility has grounded his view.

﴿Lawful and good﴾: ḥalālan (lawful) is a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) referring to the spoils that were taken, or an adjective of the verbal noun, meaning "eating that is lawful." Its benefit is to remove what had settled in their souls because of that reproach, or the scruple over it on the part of the earlier ones. For this reason He described it with His words: ﴿good﴾, ṭayyiban (good, pure). ﴿And fear God﴾: by disobeying Him. ﴿Surely God is Forgiving﴾: He has forgiven your sin, ﴿Merciful﴾: He has permitted you what you took.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 70–71:

﴿O Prophet, say to those among your captives: …﴾ Abu 'Amr recited "min al-asra" (مَنِ الأسارى) instead of "min al-asra" (مِنَ الأسْرى) [i.e., with the variant reading of the preposition and the plural form of "captives"]. ﴿If Allah knows any good in your hearts﴾ — faith and sincerity. ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾ — from the ransom.

It was narrated that it was revealed concerning al-'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had charged to ransom himself and his two nephews, 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib and Nawfal ibn al-Harith. He said: "O Muhammad, you have left me to beg from Quraysh for as long as I live." He said: "Where is the gold that you gave to Umm al-Fadl when you set out, and you said to her: 'I do not know what may befall me on this journey; if some misfortune happens to me, then it is yours and that of 'Abd Allah, 'Ubayd Allah, al-Fadl and Qutham'?" Al-'Abbas said: "How could you know that?" He said: "My Lord, the Exalted, informed me of it." He said: "I bear witness that you are truthful, and that there is no god but Allah, and that you are His Messenger. By Allah, no one knew of it except Allah, and I handed it to her in the darkness of the night." Al-'Abbas said: "Allah replaced it for me with something better: now I have twenty slaves, the least of whom trades with twenty thousand, and He has given me Zamzam, which I would not want to exchange for all the wealth of the people of Makkah. And I am awaiting forgiveness from your Lord," meaning the promise in His words: ﴿and He will forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

﴿And if they intend﴾ — meaning the captives — ﴿treachery against you﴾ — breaking what they pledged to you. ﴿Then they have already betrayed Allah﴾ — by disbelief and breaking His covenant, which was taken by reason. ﴿before, so He gave you power over them﴾ — i.e., He gave you power over them as He did on the day of Badr. So if they return to treachery, He will give you power over them again. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 72–73:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated﴾ are the emigrants (al-muhajirun), who left their homelands out of love for Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And strove with their wealth and their selves in the way of Allah﴾: they spent their wealth on horses and weapons and gave it to the needy, and ﴿with their selves﴾ by engaging directly in fighting. ﴿And those who gave shelter and helped﴾ are the Helpers (al-Ansar), who sheltered the emigrants in their homes and helped them against their enemies. ﴿Those are allies of one another﴾ in inheritance. The emigrants and the Helpers used to inherit from one another by virtue of emigration and support, to the exclusion of relatives, until this was abrogated (nusikha) by His saying:

﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another﴾ [Q 8:75], or in support and backing.

﴿As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of allegiance to them at all until they emigrate﴾, i.e., regarding their inheritance. Hamza read ﴿wilayatihim﴾ with a kasra (wilayatihim, as opposed to walayatihim), likening it to a craft or office such as kitaba (writing) and imara (command), as if by assuming its responsibility the holder were practising a profession. ﴿And if they seek your help in religion, then it is incumbent upon you to help them﴾, meaning it is obligatory upon you to help them against the polytheists. ﴿Except against a people between you and whom there is a covenant﴾, a treaty; for their covenant is not broken by helping them against those people. ﴿And Allah is seeing of what you do﴾.

﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾ in inheritance or in mutual support. By implication, this indicates the prohibition of inheritance or support between them and the Muslims. ﴿Unless you do it﴾, i.e., unless you do what you have been commanded: maintaining ties among yourselves, and allying with one another, even in inheritance, and severing relations between yourselves and the disbelievers. ﴿There will be fitnah in the land﴾: a great fitnah will occur therein, namely the weakening of faith and the manifestation of disbelief. ﴿And great corruption﴾ in religion. It is also read as ﴿kathir﴾ (many).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 74–75:

﴿And those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped – it is they who are truly the believers.﴾ When He divided the believers into three categories, He made clear that the perfect in faith among them are those who actualized their faith by achieving its requirement of emigration (hijrah) and struggle (jihad), the expenditure of wealth, and the support of the truth. He promised them a noble reward, saying: ﴿For them is forgiveness and a generous provision﴾, which has no consequence (taba'ah) and no reproach (minnah) attached. Then He joined to them in both respects those who would later join them and take on their characteristics, saying: ﴿And those who believed afterwards, emigrated and strove alongside you – they are of you﴾, i.e., of your number, O emigrants and helpers. ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another﴾ in inheritance than strangers. ﴿In the Book of Allah﴾ – in His judgment, or in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh), or in the Qur'an. It has been used as evidence for the inheritance of distant kindred (dhawu al-arham). ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knower of all things﴾ – of the inheritances, and of the wisdom in tying them first to the bond of Islam and mutual support, and then, secondly, to the consideration of kinship.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Anfal and Bara'ah, I will be an intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection, and a witness that he is free from hypocrisy, and he will be given ten good deeds for every male and female hypocrite, and the Throne and its bearers will seek forgiveness for him during the days of his life."
